summary.name: My Philosophy on Alerting
summary.one_liner: A Google Doc by former Google Site Reliability Engineer Rob Ewaschuk describing his philosophy on monitoring and alerting, based on his SRE experience.
use_cases: Deciding what conditions should trigger pages
summary.what_it_does: The page is a written document titled "My Philosophy on Alerting" by Rob Ewaschuk, based on observations from his time as a Site Reliability Engineer at Google. The meta description lists its sections: monitoring for your users, why cause-based alerts are bad but sometimes necessary, and alerting on symptoms. The text captured here is mostly Google Docs interface content (a JavaScript notice and a Building blocks promo), so the document's actual body was not available to summarize. It is listed in the dastergon/awesome-sre list under Monitoring, Observability and Alerting.
notable: Written by a former Google SRE, Rob Ewaschuk
Argues for alerting on user-facing symptoms rather than causes
Listed in the awesome-sre resource collection
caveats: Captured page text is only interface content; the document body was not visible
Pricing is not stated on the page; the document is publicly viewable as a Google Doc
